targetReport.title: Local Non-Domestic Rating List / Council Tax Valuation List
targetReport.description: The national property-valuation function underlying both Council Tax bands and Business Rates rateable values — the UK functional equivalent of the Netherlands' `nl-wet-woz` and Ontario's `mpac-assessment`. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Finance Act 1992 ss.20-23 (Council Tax valuation lists) and Local Government Finance Act 1988 ss.41, 61 and Sch.6 (business-rates rating lists and the 'rateable value' definition). NOTE ON NAMING: neither Act uses the literal string 'Valuation Office Agency' in the sections checked — both instead say 'the Commissioners of Inland Revenue' / 'the valuation officer' / 'listing officer'. 'Valuation Office Agency' as a literal name only appears in downstream documents (see `uk-stevenage-nndr1`) — flagged per this project's own tense/naming-precision convention rather than silently modernised.
targetReport.cadence_note: Business-rates rating lists are compiled on a multi-year revaluation cycle (1988 Act s.41(2): 1 April 1990 and every fifth year after, subject to later amendment); Council Tax valuation lists are maintained continuously. Filed as annual as the nearest practical cadence.

release_schedule.rule: Non-Domestic Rating Act 2023: from Royal Assent, business rates (non-domestic rating list) revaluations occur every 3 years rather than every 5, beginning with the list compiled 1 April 2026. New rating lists are compiled and come into force on 1 April in the revaluation year.
release_schedule.note: This corpus entry appears to bundle two distinct VOA products. (1) The Local Non-Domestic Rating List (business rates) now revalues every 3 years per the Non-Domestic Rating Act 2023 (2023 -> 2026 -> next 2029); the 2026 list was already compiled/in force by 1 April 2026, before today's date (2026-08-11), so the next compiled list is due 1 April 2029. (2) The Council Tax Valuation List (domestic property bands) has no fixed statutory revaluation cycle in England (irregular, last fully revalued 1991/2003 in Wales); Wales is separately pursuing a council tax revaluation reform (targeting new valuation lists around 2028) via the Local Government Finance (Wales) Bill, but as of this research no confirmed in-force date was found for that Welsh council tax revaluation - it remains a policy proposal under legislative development, not a scheduled release. If these are meant to be split into two separate corpus entries, the non-domestic rating list has the clearer stated-rule schedule (above); the council tax valuation list would be closer to 'irregular' (England) or a not-yet-finalized reform timeline (Wales).

targetReport.title: Handbook on Residential Property Prices Indices (RPPIs)
targetReport.publisher: Eurostat, ILO, IMF, OECD, UNECE and the World Bank
targetReport.description: The international methodological handbook for residential property (house) price indices, 2013 edition, published by Eurostat (catalogue KS-RA-12-022) and copyrighted jointly by the European Union, the International Labour Organization, the International Monetary Fund, the OECD, the UN Economic Commission for Europe and the World Bank. It covers the uses of RPPIs, stratification, hedonic regression, repeat-sales and appraisal-based methods, the land/structures split, data sources and recommendations.
